latest_rss.summary:
Executive Summary:




The “life-saving chain” developed by the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) Joint Logistics Support Force (JLSF) to evacuate and treat casualties is part of the wider lessons it gained from observing the ongoing Russian war in Ukraine.



Drones and other unmanned platforms provide the JLSF units with an increased capacity to evacuate wounded personnel to field hospitals and other medical sites for treatment.



The use of intelligent equipment such as electronic casualty tags and telemedicine surgery capabilities enhances the JLSF’s ability to effectively treat wounded personnel.



The JLSF’s live-saving chain would likely face some limitations, such as developing an overreliance on unmanned platforms that can be jammed, and which emit substantial electromagnetic signatures that can assist targeting.

latest_rss.title: Russia and Pakistan Sign Deal on Rail Connectivity
latest_rss.summary:
Executive Summary:




Pakistan and Russia signed a freight-forwarding contract on August 31 to establish a framework for international freight transportation and pursue a pilot container train linking Pakistan with Russia, Central Asia, and possibly Belarus.



Earlier efforts to launch the connection have been repeatedly delayed, including a planned June 2025 pilot that was cancelled amid conflict in Iran. Each proposed route would transit Iran, with options discussed through Central Asia or Azerbaijan.



The project faces significant infrastructure and security challenges, including Iran’s incomplete rail links, differing railway standards, and instability along proposed routes. If completed, it could expand Russia’s access to South Asia and Pakistani ports.

latest_rss.title: Hungary’s Ukraine Reset Off to a Shaky Start
latest_rss.summary:
Executive Summary:




Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar initially aimed for a quick reset with Ukraine by unblocking Kyiv’s EU accession talks in exchange for a bilateral deal on protecting and expanding the rights of ethnic Hungarians in Ukraine.  



The bilateral relationship has seen major setbacks in recent weeks over Hungary’s refusal to advance Ukraine’s EU accession talks, Magyar saying that a Ukrainian petroleum storage facility would not be built in Hungary under Tisza rule, and Budapest’s decision not to join the Carpathian Eight, a new Ukraine-led regional cooperation format. 



Future Hungary–Ukraine relations will be defined by Ukraine’s implementation of the minority rights agreement, with legislative progress expected in October. A failure to implement the deal could risk slowing down Kyiv’s EU path and decoupling the Ukrainian and Moldovan accession bids.

latest_rss.title: Having Lost ‘Presidents,’ Ever More Russian Federal Subjects Now Have Prime Ministers
latest_rss.summary:
Executive Summary:




At Russian President Vladimir Putin’s insistence, Russia has only one president. Since his war against Ukraine began in 2022, the number of federal subjects with prime ministers in addition to Moscow-appointed “heads” has risen from 10 to 39 and is likely to continue to rise.



This change, which has largely been under the radar, reflects the increasing burdens Putin’s policies have shifted to the federal subjects and the desire of their heads to share these and the challenges anger about them now pose.



As a result, the governments of the federal subjects are looking like self-standing institutions even though Moscow appoints their heads and thus may have a greater capacity to act as independent actors in the course of the looming succession struggle.
